newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: DBS says ready to offer Thailand credit.
newsitem.headline: DBS says ready to offer Thailand credit.

text.p: The Development Bank of Singapore (DBS) is in touch with Thailand on the possibility of offering it emergency credit lines, DBS president Ng Kee Choe said on Wednesday.

"We are in touch with officials there. If there is a need, we will look at it in the most positive manner," Ng told Reuters after a press briefing on the bank's earnings for six months ended June 1997. He declined to give further details.
Earlier on Wednesday, Thai Finance Minister Thanong Bidaya said Bangkok had received numerous offers of emergency credit lines from many foreign commercial lenders.
But Thanong said Thailand had its own resources and money was not the problem.
Ng said the bank's exposure to potentially bad Thai debts was "relatively small" and "negligible".

He said there was no need to be concerned over the banks's Thai exposure as the Bangkok government would effectively guarantee all debtors and depositors of the 42 finance companies whose operations it suspended on Tuesday.
Ng said debts of the finance companies not suspended were protected by a Federal Insurance Scheme.

"So the situation in Thailand is now resolved," Ng said. "We are not concern at all, primarily because we are well provisioned and effectively guaranteed by the Thai government." DBS has loans out to five of the 42 finance firms.
Ng dismissed a UBS report that DBS has a net exposure of about Singapore $1.02 billion in Thai loans.
On DBS plans to buy a 60 percent stake in Thailand's Sri Dhana Finance Public Company Ltd, Ng said:
"We are still at due deligence stage which will take some time to finish. The outcome of the MOU (Memorandum of Understanding) will depend on the due deligence which is in progress," Ng said.
The suspension of Sri Dhana would not have any impact on the DBS plan to take a stake, he added.
"Its assets, liabilities have all been taken into consideration by the due deligence," Ng said, adding the due deligence was expected to be completed in two months.
Ng said DBS expansion plans in Thailand and the region would not be affected by Thailand's economic crisis.

"I think we should not be distracted by short term developments. We are long term players. In the long term, we are confident about the growth prospects in the region and there are opportunities," he said.
Ng said he expected revenue from DBS overseas operations would continue to see "steady growth".
